svg.text: K1b CEILING TURRET CELL — one hand, food beside it, never under it
One ceiling turret (disc, rod, elbow arm, magnet roll); turning hobs, a lever dicer and a spindle; one well washes all.
7 actuators (hand 4, T0, H1, spindle) · 2 dynamic seals
est. cost ≈ 10.3 k€ machine + 1.95 k€ bought · oven outside
TOP VIEW at the deck (z 850) — the turret works in polar coordinates
under two lids, combs at both sides

g.text: lever dicer on its stand, over T0

svg.text: seam circle r 225: no open food inside
THE HAND (all 4 drives in the dry drive room)
D disc Ø 420 turns in the ceiling (dashed grey circle)
Z rod Ø 50 slides 440 mm; a load cell weighs every grip ±10 g
Y rod turns = elbow: tool reaches 185–535 mm from C (orange rings)
K roll at the arm tip through a canned magnet coupling
All tools hang on the roll sleeve by one stub (Ø 22, 60° lock)
Beside, never under: open food only outside the seam circle
Force and time from stations: turning T0/H1, dicer, spindle
Ware never leaves the cell: washed and stored in the well
Retract before the door: rod up, arm folded over the well
Clean 20 min (2 p) / 33 min (4 p) after hand-over · ≈ 39 L

g.text: 1/8 Box in: the transport puts an opened box of mince on the port drawer; the hand takes its stub, pours it into the bowl on T0 and weighs the loss (load cell)
2/8 Peeling: the spit takes a potato from the nest, the roll spins it while the arm draws it past the peeler post; peel drops into the dump slot; potato into the pot on H2
3/8 Dicing: the lever dicer is set over the bowl on T0; the arm presses the lever pad 200 mm down (300 N × 7 ≈ 2 kN): onion halves become 6 mm dice
4/8 Herbs and kneading: the spindle chops parsley in the jug; the jug is poured; T0 turns the bowl at 40 rpm under the kneading roller, the hand is free
5/8 Frying: the disher takes 110 g balls (weighed by Z) round the front, outside the seam circle, into the pan on H1; the presser smashes them flat
6/8 Turning: the turner slides under each patty, lifts 30 mm and rolls 180°; core probe 72 °C; the potatoes boil on H2
7/8 Plating by polar placement: bowl into the well, a warm plate comes in; T0 turns it so each spot lies under the arm; patty, potatoes, sauce arc; out through the port
8/8 Washing under the turret: lids lifted, pan and pot hung on the combs; cold rinse, 60 °C wash, 88 °C rinse (A0 ≥ 90), dry; the closed well is the clean store
